Ran 31 commands, read memory, and 2 more tools
Phase 19 is in positional-phase19.tar.gz, which has 20 files (19 changed, 1 new). Extract it at the repo root, then delete the two files it replaces:

sh
git rm app/src/main/java/app/simple/positional/util/ReverseGeocoder.kt app/src/main/java/app/simple/positional/util/StatusBarHeight.kt
What changed

Sensors: the heading and level sensors now get the screen rotation through ContextCompat.getDisplayOrDefault. The deprecated defaultDisplay and WindowManager are no longer used.
Status bar height: it now comes from the window insets in BaseActivity, instead of the internal Android resource that lint discourages. setPositionalContent moved into BaseActivity.
Geocoding: a new Geocoding object handles both address lookup and map search. Map search now uses the app language and no longer crashes on a geocoder error on Android 13+.
Network check: it now asks the active network whether it has internet. The deprecated NetworkInfo fallback is gone, since minSdk 24 doesn’t need it.
Web view: I removed the force dark fallback, because it does nothing on target SDK 33+. The class is now final, so its warning suppression is gone too.
Preferences: a custom location or direction target is now saved in one apply call. It used to be several separate commits, so other parts of the app could briefly see half a location. The unused single-value setters were removed.
Dead code removed: unused math helpers and CompassAzimuth.inverse. round now uses roundToLong, so large values can’t overflow. The tests are updated to match.
README: phase 19 is marked done. Phase 20 is next: remove unused resources and enforce the lint UnusedResources check in CI.
The suppressions I kept are the old blocking Geocoder calls (needed below Android 13), MissingPermission, ViewConstructor and ApplySharedPref-free preferences.

I could only check the syntax here, so CI will do the real compile and test run.

Worth checking on the Nord

Rotate the phone to landscape on the compass and level panels. North and the bubble should stay correct.
The toolbar should still sit just below the status bar on every panel and sub screen. Watch for a one-frame jump at launch.
Pick a custom location, and pick a direction target. Each should apply right away.
Run a map search with internet on, then off.
